public_rationale: On 18 February 2024, Marcus wrote that at least one person had been fooled by a Sora video and that "he won't be the last." This forecast is supported. On 24 November 2025, The Canadian Press reported that videos made with the Sora 2 app "have fooled many internet users since the app launched in September." That report is dated after the post, so it meets the contract's rule for early resolution. A HuffPost article published 14 November 2025 adds more limited support. It says Facebook users were "being duped" by AI-generated ICE raid videos and that one such clip was "likely generated by OpenAI's Sora."
limitations: The Canadian Press makes a general statement. It does not name or count the people who were fooled.
HuffPost says the ICE clip was likely made with Sora. It does not say this for certain.
Both reports concern Sora 2, a later version than the Sora model in Marcus's post.
The Canadian Press piece also discusses videos from other AI models.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: More people besides the one already fooled will be fooled by fake Sora-generated videos.

statement.excerpt: I guarantee he won’t be the last:

our_interpretation: Read plainly: after the post, other people would be fooled by fake videos made with Sora, meaning they would take them as real.
criteria.support_condition: A credible, dated report after 2024-02-18 that people took Sora-generated videos for real footage.
criteria.contradiction_condition: No real way to falsify this before the tool is gone. Lasting absence of any documented cases would count against it.
